subject.title: fix(mcp): MCP disabled: true silently ignored — gateway spawns server processes anyway

question: Should OpenClaw deliberately add a server-level `disabled` MCP alias that neither the shipped OpenClaw contract nor current Codex supports?
rationale: This is a permanent public configuration and precedence decision rather than a dependency-backed repair, so implementation alone cannot determine the supported contract.

options.title: Keep `enabled` canonical
options.body: Reject the alias and direct unsupported `disabled` input to `enabled: false` or `openclaw mcp configure <name> --disable`.

options.title: Formalize the alias
options.body: Approve an OpenClaw-specific alias, preserve explicit `enabled`, and update types, schema/help, docs, diagnostics, upgrade behavior, tests, and live proof.

recommendation.title: Keep `enabled` canonical
recommendation.body: Reject the alias and direct unsupported `disabled` input to `enabled: false` or `openclaw mcp configure <name> --disable`.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged operator-workflow changes established the current public MCP activation contract.
